_qms_instructions.purpose: Single Source of Truth for NHS Ayrshire & Arran Microbiology Test Directory (PDM-ATH020-WEB).
_qms_instructions.how_to_update: 1. Update 'qmsMetadata' (handbookVersion, effectiveDate, nextReviewDate, approvedBy). 2. Edit/add entries in 'tests'. 3. Validate JSON syntax before uploading alongside index.html to AthenA/web server.

field_reference.name: Primary display name of the investigation
field_reference.trakCode: Exact OrderComms / TrakCare test description (Appendix 2 or Referral)
field_reference.category: One of the primary clinical categories
field_reference.containerColor: Visual badge key: blue-bc, purple-bc, pink-bc, universal, boricon, baby-boricon, emu, yellow-sputum, blue-faeces, black-swab, blue-swab, orange-swab, multicollect, mss, serum, edta, lihe, acanthamoeba, dry-pack
field_reference.consultantDiscussion: Boolean: true if duty microbiologist approval is required before sampling/testing
field_reference.urgentOOH: Boolean: true if available urgently out-of-hours
field_reference.noPneumaticTube: Boolean: true if strictly prohibited from pneumatic tube transport
field_reference.clinicalDetailsRequired: Mandatory clinical information required on request form
field_reference.rejectionTriggers: Array of common pre-analytical reasons this sample will be rejected
field_reference.collectionNotes: Step-by-step sampling, handling, and storage guidance
field_reference.synonyms: Array of search keywords, pathogens, or clinical terms

qmsMetadata.sourceHandbookTitle: NHS Ayrshire & Arran Microbiology User Handbook
qmsMetadata.approvedBy: Consultant Medical Microbiologist / Microbiology Quality Lead

labContacts.oohCsfBms: Via Crosshouse Switchboard (22:00-09:00 Urgent CSF Only)

tests.name: Blood Culture - Adult
tests.container: Adult Blood Culture Set (Blue Aerobic + Purple Anaerobic bottles)
tests.sampleType: Venous blood (8-10 mL per bottle)
tests.tat: Preliminary negative: 48h | Final negative: 5 days (7 days if endocarditis stated) | Positives phoned immediately; RAST 20:00-21:00
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Signs of sepsis, focus of infection, current/proposed antibiotics, prosthetic material/suspected endocarditis (for 7-day incubation).
rejectionTriggers: Sent via pneumatic tube system (strictly prohibited)
Non-sterile site fluid inoculated into blood culture bottles
Missing clinical justification or patient CHI/identifiers
tests.collectionNotes: Collect BEFORE starting or changing antimicrobials using strict aseptic technique. Inoculate blue-top aerobic bottle first, then purple-top anaerobic bottle. Transport to Crosshouse within 4 hours at ambient temperature.

tests.name: Blood Culture - Paediatric
tests.container: Paediatric Blood Culture Bottle (Pink top BD BACTEC Peds Plus)
tests.sampleType: Venous blood
tests.tat: Neonates preliminary negative: 24h | Children preliminary negative: 48h | Final negative: 5 days
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Clinical signs of sepsis, age, focus of infection, antibiotic exposure.
rejectionTriggers: Sent via pneumatic tube system
Missing clinical details or incomplete labelling
tests.collectionNotes: Strict aseptic technique before antibiotics. Send immediately to Crosshouse (within 4 hours). Do not refrigerate.

tests.name: Mycobacterial Blood / Bone Marrow Culture
tests.referralLab: Scottish Mycobacterial Reference Laboratory (SMRL), Royal Infirmary Edinburgh
tests.container: Specific TB Blood Culture Bottle (obtain from Microbiology Lab)
tests.sampleType: Blood or bone marrow aspirate
tests.tat: Up to 12 weeks for final negative report
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Immunocompromise status (e.g. advanced HIV), suspected disseminated mycobacterial infection, travel/exposure history.
rejectionTriggers: Requested without prior Consultant Microbiologist approval
Standard blood culture bottles used instead of lab-issued TB bottles
tests.collectionNotes: Only available after discussion with Consultant Microbiologist. Specific bottles are stocked only in the Crosshouse laboratory.

tests.name: CSF Microscopy, Cell Count & Culture
tests.container: 3 x Sterile Universal Containers (white/clear top, 20 mL, numbered 1-3 in order of draw)
tests.sampleType: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)
tests.volume: 3-5 mL total across 3 numbered universal containers
tests.tat: Microscopy/Cell count: 1 hour from receipt | Culture: 24-48 hours
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Suspected meningitis/encephalitis, onset, immunosuppression, recent neurosurgery/shunt, antibiotic therapy.
rejectionTriggers: Sent via pneumatic tube system
Delayed arrival (>2 hours degrades cell count accuracy)
OOH sample sent without prior registrar/consultant decision and switchboard alert to on-call BMS
tests.collectionNotes: URGENT: Notify lab once taken. Must arrive within 2 hours. OOH (22:00-09:00): Registrar/Consultant decision required; contact on-call BMS via switchboard ONLY once sample is taken. Arrange urgent porter/taxi. Lymphocytic CSFs are automatically forwarded to WoSSVC for viral PCR.

tests.name: CSF Bacterial & Viral PCR Panel
tests.referralLab: West of Scotland Specialist Virology Centre / SMRL, Glasgow Royal Infirmary
tests.container: Sterile Universal Container (white top) + concurrent EDTA blood if meningococcal disease suspected
tests.sampleType: CSF (and EDTA blood for meningococcal PCR)
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Clinical suspicion of viral/bacterial meningitis or encephalitis, CSF cell count, prior antibiotics.
rejectionTriggers: Insufficient CSF volume remaining after microscopy/culture
tests.collectionNotes: Predominantly lymphocytic CSFs are automatically forwarded to WoSSVC for viral PCR (HSV, VZV, Enterovirus, Parechovirus). If meningococcal infection is suspected, also send an EDTA blood sample requesting meningococcal PCR.

tests.name: CSF Mycobacterial (TB) Microscopy, Culture & PCR
tests.referralLab: Scottish Mycobacterial Reference Laboratory (SMRL), Royal Infirmary Edinburgh
tests.container: Sterile Universal Container (white top, additive-free)
tests.sampleType: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)
tests.tat: AAFB Microscopy: 2 working days | PCR: Rapid on SMRL discretion | Culture: Up to 8-12 weeks
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Suspected TB meningitis, risk factors/exposure, HIV/immunosuppression status, basal enhancement/hydrocephalus.
rejectionTriggers: Volume < 6 mL
Not discussed with Consultant Microbiologist in advance
tests.collectionNotes: Discuss with Consultant Microbiologist BEFORE lumbar puncture so an adequate volume (>=6 mL) is collected.

tests.name: CSF Spongiform Encephalopathy (CJD / 14-3-3 / RT-QuIC)
tests.referralLab: National CJD Research & Surveillance Unit, Edinburgh University
tests.container: Sterile Universal Container (white top)
tests.sampleType: Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF)
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Rapidly progressive dementia/neurological decline, neurology review, prior NCJDRSU approval reference.
rejectionTriggers: Taken out-of-hours or at weekends (strictly prohibited due to freezing/transport rules)
No prior approval from NCJDRSU and Consultant Microbiologist
tests.collectionNotes: Requires prior approval from NCJDRSU and advance coordination with Consultant Microbiologist. Sampling CANNOT take place outwith core working hours or at weekends.

tests.name: Faeces Investigation - Routine Enteric Culture
tests.container: Blue-capped Faeces Container with spoon
tests.sampleType: Liquid/soft diarrhoeal stool (taking shape of pot)
tests.volume: At least 1/4 full (include mucus, pus, or blood)
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Acute diarrhoea (<14 days, >=3 soft stools/day), travel history, occupation (food handler/healthcare), outbreak/HUS suspicion.
rejectionTriggers: Received > 72 hours after collection
Repeat sample within 7 days
Chronic diarrhoea or formed stool without justification
tests.collectionNotes: Screens for Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, and E. coli O157. Once diarrhoea has stopped, culture is no longer indicated. Refrigerate if transport delayed.

tests.name: Clostridioides difficile Testing (GDH Screen & Toxin ELISA)
tests.container: Blue-capped Faeces Container with spoon
tests.sampleType: Unformed/diarrhoeal stool ONLY (patients >= 3 years old)
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Diarrhoea history, recent/current antibiotic exposure, inpatient/care home status.
rejectionTriggers: Solid/formed stool (automatically rejected)
Patient < 3 years of age
Repeat within 28 days of a confirmed positive result
tests.collectionNotes: Tested automatically on diarrhoeal samples in patients >= 3 years. Do not send test-of-cure samples after treatment.

tests.name: Faeces Parasitology (Ova, Cysts & Parasites / Cryptosporidium)
tests.container: Blue-capped Faeces Container with spoon (Note: Sellotape slide for Enterobius)
tests.sampleType: Faeces (2 consecutive days; max 3 samples)
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: MANDATORY: Specific foreign travel history, prolonged diarrhoea, or contact with confirmed intestinal parasite.
rejectionTriggers: No travel or parasite contact history provided
Faeces sent for threadworm (Enterobius vermicularis) - requires Sellotape slide
tests.collectionNotes: Not performed routinely—must be specifically requested with travel/exposure details. For threadworm, request Sellotape slide kit from specimen reception.

tests.name: Faeces Norovirus / Enterovirus / Coxsackie PCR
tests.referralLab: West of Scotland Specialist Virology Centre, Glasgow Royal Infirmary
tests.container: Blue-capped Faeces Container with spoon
tests.sampleType: Faeces (stool)
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Acute vomiting/diarrhoea, ward/care home outbreak details, immunocompromise.
rejectionTriggers: Missing clinical/outbreak details
tests.collectionNotes: Send fresh diarrhoeal stool. Inform Infection Prevention & Control if ward outbreak suspected.

tests.name: Respiratory Conventional Bacterial Culture (Sputum / ETA / BAL)
tests.trakCode: Sputum (Routine Culture) / Bronchial Washings / Nasopharyngeal Aspirate
tests.container: Yellow-capped wide-mouth Sputum Container (or White Universal for BAL/ETA)
tests.sampleType: Deep expectorated sputum, ETA, or BAL
tests.volume: Sputum: min 1 mL | BAL: min 5 mL
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Lower respiratory tract signs, pneumonia/COPD exacerbation, ICU/ventilation status, cystic fibrosis/bronchiectasis, antibiotics.
rejectionTriggers: Salivary or postnasal specimens (automatically rejected)
Received > 72 hours after collection
Repeat sputum within 3 days
tests.collectionNotes: Collect deep lower respiratory tract specimen before antibiotics. Refrigerate if transport delayed up to 24h. Multiple BAL samples will be pooled unless agreed with Microbiologist.

tests.name: Respiratory Mycobacterial (TB) Culture & AAFB Microscopy
tests.location: In-House (Crosshouse) / Referred to SMRL if smear positive or PCR approved
tests.referralLab: Scottish Mycobacterial Reference Laboratory (SMRL), Edinburgh (for rapid PCR/ID)
tests.container: Yellow-capped wide-mouth Sputum Container (or Universal for BAL/biopsy)
tests.sampleType: Early morning sputum (x3 consecutive days), ETA, BAL, or pleural biopsy
tests.volume: Sputum: min 1 mL x 3 | BAL: min 5 mL
tests.tat: AAFB microscopy: 2 working days | Local culture: up to 8 weeks | Referred culture: up to 12 weeks
tests.resamplingInterval: Send 3 early morning samples on consecutive days (>=8-24h apart)
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Suspected pulmonary TB, radiological findings, weight loss/night sweats/haemoptysis, HIV/immunosuppression, contact history.
rejectionTriggers: Saliva/postnasal secretions
Samples taken <8 hours apart (will be pooled)
Direct TB PCR requested without Consultant Physician/Microbiologist discussion
tests.collectionNotes: Collect 3 early morning purulent sputum samples on consecutive days before TB therapy. Note: Pleural fluid has low sensitivity for TB; pleural biopsy is preferred. Fast-track TB PCR requires consultant discussion.

tests.name: Pneumocystis jirovecii (PCP) PCR
tests.referralLab: Scottish Parasite Diagnostic and Reference Lab, Glasgow Royal Infirmary
tests.container: Yellow-capped Sputum Container or White Universal Container (BAL/ETA)
tests.sampleType: BAL, ETA, or deep induced sputum
tests.volume: BAL: min 5 mL | Sputum: min 1 mL
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: MANDATORY: Specific nature of patient's immunocompromise (e.g., HIV/CD4 count, chemotherapy, high-dose steroids, transplant) and hypoxia/CXR findings.
rejectionTriggers: Nature of immunocompromise not stated on request
Throat swab sent instead of lower respiratory tract specimen
tests.collectionNotes: BAL is the optimal sample type; induced sputum/ETA accepted. Throat swabs are NOT suitable.

tests.name: Multiplex Respiratory Viral PCR (COVID-19, Flu A/B, RSV)
tests.container: Molecular Sampling Solution (MSS - red-capped vial; REMOVE SWAB after swirling)
tests.sampleType: Combined throat and nose swab in MSS
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Acute respiratory symptoms, inpatient/admission status, IPC/cohorting requirement.
rejectionTriggers: SWAB LEFT INSIDE THE MSS VIAL (automatically rejected)
Received >= 72 hours after specimen collection
Duplicate sample sent on same testing occasion
tests.collectionNotes: Swab throat and nose with dry swab, swirl in MSS fluid for 30 seconds, express against vial wall, and DISCARD THE SWAB before capping tightly.

tests.name: Extended Respiratory PCR Panel (ICU / Immunocompromised Only)
tests.referralLab: West of Scotland Specialist Virology Centre, Glasgow Royal Infirmary
tests.container: MSS vial (throat/nose swab) OR Universal/Sputum pot (BAL/ETA/NPA/Sputum)
tests.sampleType: Throat swab in MSS, NPA, BAL, ETA, or sputum
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: MANDATORY: Confirm patient is in Critical Care (ICU/HDU) OR immunocompromised.
rejectionTriggers: Requested for non-immunocompromised general ward or GP patient
Swab left inside MSS vial
tests.collectionNotes: Includes Flu A/B, RSV, Rhinovirus/Enterovirus, Adenovirus, Parainfluenza 1-4, HMPV, Seasonal Coronaviruses, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and SARS-CoV-2.

tests.name: Bordetella pertussis (Whooping Cough) PCR
tests.referralLab: West of Scotland Specialist Virology Centre, Glasgow Royal Infirmary
tests.container: Molecular Sampling Solution (MSS - red-capped vial; REMOVE SWAB)
tests.sampleType: Combined nose and throat swab (or nasopharyngeal swab) in MSS
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Duration of paroxysmal cough (<2-3 weeks for PCR), apnoea/whoop, infant/pregnancy contact, vaccination history.
rejectionTriggers: Swab left inside MSS vial
Black charcoal bacterial swab sent instead of MSS
tests.collectionNotes: Preferred diagnostic test in first 2-3 weeks of cough. Notify Public Health on clinical suspicion. For cough >3 weeks, Pertussis serology (white-top serum) may be used for retrospective diagnosis.

tests.name: Urine - Conventional Bacterial Culture (& Paed Microscopy)
tests.trakCode: Urine Culture / Urine Microscopy (Auto added to Paed patients)
tests.container: Red-topped Boricon Container (20 mL adult; 7 mL Baby Boricon for low volume/paeds)
tests.sampleType: MSU, CSU, Clean Catch (CCU), SPA, Nephrostomy/Urostomy
tests.volume: Fill strictly to the fill line on Boricon label
tests.tat: Negative: 24 hours | Positive: 48 hours | Paed microscopy: 24 hours
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Clinical signs/symptoms of UTI, specific specimen type (MSU/CSU/CCU/SPA), pregnancy status, antibiotic therapy.
rejectionTriggers: Sent in white-top universal container (automatically rejected for culture)
Under-filled Boricon tube (boric acid becomes bactericidal)
Sampled from catheter collection bag or bedpan
Asymptomatic screening or repeat within 3 days
tests.collectionNotes: Do NOT discard boric acid powder. Fill to line and mix gently. Do NOT refrigerate Boricon tubes. Microscopy is ONLY performed routinely in children <16 years (urgent OOH paed microscopy available 17:00-21:00 weekdays & 09:00-21:00 weekends via on-call BMS).

tests.name: Urine Mycobacterial (Renal TB) Culture
tests.referralLab: Scottish Mycobacterial Reference Laboratory (SMRL), Royal Infirmary Edinburgh
tests.container: Silver-capped 160 mL Early Morning Urine (EMU) Container (request from Lab)
tests.sampleType: Entire early morning urine void on 3 consecutive days
tests.volume: Full first morning void x 3 days (do not pool)
tests.tat: Up to 12 weeks for final negative report
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Sterile pyuria, suspected renal/genitourinary TB, TB exposure/history.
rejectionTriggers: Sent in Boricon (boric acid) container
Pooled urine specimens
tests.collectionNotes: Request specific 160 mL preservative-free EMU containers from Microbiology. Collect entire early morning urine on 3 consecutive days. Microscopy is NOT performed on urine for TB.

tests.name: Urinary Legionella & Pneumococcal Antigens
tests.trakCode: Legionella Urinary Antigen / Pneumo/Legionella Urinary Antigen (ITU/HDU only)
tests.container: Red-topped Boricon OR White-topped Universal Container
tests.sampleType: Urine
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Severe community-acquired pneumonia (CURB-65 >=3 / ICU / HDU), travel/spa/water exposure history.
rejectionTriggers: Pneumococcal urinary antigen requested outside Critical Care/HDU without Consultant Microbiologist approval
Routine Legionella testing in mild-moderate CAP without risk factors
tests.collectionNotes: Pneumococcal antigen is restricted to Critical Care/HDU patients or following Consultant Microbiologist discussion. Legionella antigen detects L. pneumophila serogroup 1.

tests.name: Bacterial Culture Swab (Wound / Ulcer / Throat / Eye / Ear / Genital)
tests.trakCode: Swab - General Culture / Wound / Throat / Ear / Eye / Vaginal (HVS/LVS/Cervical)
tests.container: Black-capped Charcoal Swab (Orange wire swab for ENT clinic ear swabs only)
tests.sampleType: Swab of leading edge of infected wound/mucosa
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Anatomical site (including Left/Right), clinical signs of active infection (cellulitis, purulence, pyrexia), current/planned antibiotics.
rejectionTriggers: Missing clinical signs of infection (surveillance swabs of non-infected ulcers rejected)
HVS samples not meeting local testing algorithm criteria
Blue-top MRSA swab used for general culture
tests.collectionNotes: Clean superficial exudate first and swab the leading edge of active infection. Note: If frank pus is present, aspirate into a white-top universal container rather than sending a swab.

tests.name: MRSA Screening Swabs
tests.container: Blue-capped Transwab (clear Amies gel)
tests.sampleType: Nasal, perineal/groin, throat, or wound/device site swabs
tests.tat: Negative: 1 working day | Positive: 2 working days
tests.resamplingInterval: Per NHS A&A IPC admission/pre-op screening policy
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Screening indication (admission, pre-operative, high-risk specialty, known previous MRSA).
rejectionTriggers: Black charcoal swab used instead of blue-capped Transwab
tests.collectionNotes: Blue-capped Transwabs are for MRSA screening ONLY. Positive screens are telephoned to clinical areas by laboratory staff.

tests.name: Carbapenemase-Producing Organism (CPE) / ESBL / VRE Screen
tests.trakCode: Screening Sample (Carbapenem-Resistant Organism (CPE) Screen) / (ESBL, GAS, S.aureus & VRE)
tests.container: Black-capped Charcoal Swab (rectal swab with visible faecal staining) or Faeces Pot
tests.sampleType: Rectal swab or faeces
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Hospitalisation abroad or outside NHS A&A in past 12 months, known CPE/VRE contact, ICU/haematology admission.
rejectionTriggers: Unstained dry rectal swab without faecal material
tests.collectionNotes: Ensure rectal swab has visible faecal staining for valid CPE/VRE screening.

tests.name: Sterile Site Aspirates, Fluids, Pus, Tissue, CVC Tips & IUCDs
tests.trakCode: Pus / Fluid (Non Pleural) / Fluid (Pleural Culture) / Fluid (CAPD Only) / Tissue Culture / IUCD Culture
tests.container: White-topped Sterile Universal Container (20 mL, NO formalin/saline)
tests.sampleType: Joint aspirate, ascitic/pleural/pericardial fluid, pus, deep tissue, bone, CVC tip, IUCD
tests.volume: Fluids/Pus: min 1-5 mL | Tissue: pea-sized piece
tests.tat: Microscopy: 24 hours (Urgent OOH 16:00-21:00 weekdays & 09:00-21:00 weekends) | Culture: 3 working days (extended if prosthetic/bone)
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Exact anatomical site, native vs prosthetic joint/implant, clinical signs of infection, antibiotics.
rejectionTriggers: Sent in formalin (kills all organisms)
Non-repeatable sterile sample sent via pneumatic tube
Syringe/needle attached to container (sharp hazard - rejected)
tests.collectionNotes: Strict aseptic technique. NEVER add formalin or saline. Do NOT send syringes/needles. Urgent sterile site aspirate microscopy (cell count & Gram stain) is available 16:00-21:00 Mon-Fri and 09:00-21:00 Sat-Sun—notify lab by phone.

tests.name: Corneal Scrapings, Vitreous Fluid & Acanthamoeba PCR
tests.referralLab: Scottish Parasite Diagnostic and Reference Lab, Glasgow Royal Infirmary (for Acanthamoeba)
tests.container: White Universal Container (scrapes/vitreous/contact lens) OR Lab-issued Acanthamoeba PCR Buffer Tube
tests.sampleType: Corneal epithelium scrape, vitreous fluid, contact lenses/case fluid
tests.volume: Maximal corneal epithelium deposited into buffer
tests.tat: Culture: 3 working days | Acanthamoeba PCR: Referred (3-5 working days)
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Contact lens wearer, keratitis/corneal ulcer, water/hot tub exposure, prior topical antimicrobials.
rejectionTriggers: Needles or blades left inside universal or buffer tubes (sharps hazard)
Acanthamoeba requested without contacting lab in advance for buffer tube
tests.collectionNotes: Contact Microbiology BEFORE sampling for Acanthamoeba to obtain the 0.25 mL PCR buffer tube. Swirl 21G needle in buffer to deposit corneal epithelium, then DISCARD needle safely. Contact lenses/fluid go in a plain white universal container.

tests.name: Superficial Mycology (Skin Scrapings, Nail Clippings & Hair)
tests.container: Folded black/dark paper packet (MycoTrans/Dermapak) or White Universal Container
tests.sampleType: Skin scrapings, full-thickness nail clippings/crumbly subungual debris, scalp scrapings/hair stumps
tests.tat: Microscopy: 5 working days | Culture: 28 working days
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: MANDATORY: Contact clinical microbiology email inbox first (available case-by-case). State site, clinical appearance, prior antifungals, animal contact.
rejectionTriggers: Sent without prior case-by-case agreement via clinical microbiology email inbox
Cut hair shafts without scalp scales/roots
Insufficient material (<5p piece size)
tests.collectionNotes: Currently available on a case-by-case basis only—contact the clinical microbiology email inbox before sending. Clean skin/nail with 70% alcohol first; scrape active advancing edge.

tests.name: Invasive Fungal Biomarkers (Beta-D-Glucan, Galactomannan, Cryptococcal Ag)
tests.trakCode: BD glucan / Systemic Aspergillus antigen / Cryptococcal antigen test
tests.referralLab: UKHSA Mycology Reference Lab Bristol / Mycology GRI
tests.container: 5.5 mL White-topped Serum Monovette (no anticoagulant) [BAL also accepted for Aspergillus Ag]
tests.sampleType: Clotted blood (serum) [or BAL for Aspergillus galactomannan]
tests.resamplingInterval: Twice weekly monitoring in high-risk haematology/ICU if indicated
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Immunosuppression (neutropenia, haematological malignancy, ICU, HIV/CD4), CT chest findings, current antifungal therapy.
rejectionTriggers: Missing immunosuppression/clinical context
tests.collectionNotes: Beta-D-Glucan and Candida antigen go to UKHSA Bristol; Systemic Aspergillus antigen goes to Mycology GRI; Cryptococcal antigen goes to UKHSA South West Bristol.

tests.name: Blood Borne Virus (BBV) Screen (HBsAg, HCV Ab, HIV Ag/Ab)
tests.trakCode: Blood Borne Virus Screen (HBsAg, Hep C Ab and HIV Ag/Ab)
tests.container: 5.5 mL White-topped Serum Monovette (no anticoagulant)
tests.sampleType: Clotted blood (serum)
tests.resamplingInterval: Repeat at 3 months post-exposure if within window period
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Specific clinical indication (e.g., deranged LFTs, needle-stick/exposure, risk factors). Do NOT write vague 'viral screen'.
rejectionTriggers: Vague requests such as 'viral studies' or 'liver screen' without specifying BBV/individual markers (held 7 days then discarded)
tests.collectionNotes: Includes Hepatitis B surface antigen, Hepatitis C antibody, and HIV 1+2 Ag/Ab combo. Use High Risk / Danger of Infection stickers if known/suspected BBV.

tests.name: Antenatal Serology Screen (Syphilis, Hepatitis B, HIV)
tests.trakCode: Ante Natal Screen (HBsAg, Syphilis and HIV)
tests.container: 5.5 mL White-topped Serum Monovette + Yellow ANTENATAL Request Form (LFM VIR007)
tests.sampleType: Clotted blood (serum)
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: LMP, EDD, gestational age, booking vs rash/contact follow-up.
rejectionTriggers: General request form used instead of Antenatal form (LFM VIR007) for antenatal booking
tests.collectionNotes: Booking serum is retained by the laboratory and can be retrieved for retrospective VZV/Parvovirus B19/Measles/Rubella testing if rash contact occurs later in pregnancy—phone lab before taking repeat blood.

tests.name: Acute Viral Hepatitis Investigation (HAV IgM, HBsAg, HCV Ab, HEV)
tests.trakCode: Hepatitis A Infection / Hepatitis B Current Infection (HBsAg) / Hepatitis C Antibody / Hepatitis E serology
tests.referralLab: West of Scotland Specialist Virology Centre, Glasgow Royal Infirmary (for Hepatitis E)
tests.container: 5.5 mL White-topped Serum Monovette (no anticoagulant)
tests.sampleType: Clotted blood (serum)
tests.tat: In-house (HAV IgM, HBsAg, HCV Ab): 24 hours | Referred HEV: 3-5 working days
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: MANDATORY: Specify ACUTE jaundice / ALT/AST >10x ULN vs CHRONIC deranged LFTs (>6 months), travel, shellfish, IVDU/exposure.
rejectionTriggers: Requests for 'liver screen' or 'viral screen' without specific tests
Hepatitis A IgG requested for travel/vaccine immunity (not accepted)
CMV/EBV requested for isolated hepatitis without mononucleosis symptoms
tests.collectionNotes: For acute icteric hepatitis: request HAV IgM, HBsAg, HCV Ab, and Hepatitis E serology. For chronic asymptomatic LFTs: request HBsAg and HCV Ab only. Urgent HAV IgM is available after Consultant Microbiologist discussion.

tests.name: Borrelia burgdorferi (Lyme Disease) IgG Screen & Confirmation
tests.referralLab: Virology Laboratory, Raigmore Hospital, Inverness (for reactive screen confirmation)
tests.container: 5.5 mL White-topped Serum Monovette (no anticoagulant)
tests.sampleType: Clotted blood (serum)
tests.tat: In-house screen: 24 hours | Referred confirmation: 7-14 days
tests.resamplingInterval: 4-6 weeks if early acute presentation (<4 weeks from tick bite) was seronegative
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Tick bite/outdoor exposure (e.g., Highlands/Ayrshire woodland), erythema migrans, neurological/cardiac/joint symptoms, onset date.
rejectionTriggers: Missing clinical/exposure history
tests.collectionNotes: Note: Typical erythema migrans is a clinical diagnosis and should be treated empirically without waiting for serology (antibodies may be negative in the first 4 weeks).

tests.name: Varicella Zoster (VZV), Measles & Rubella IgG (Immunity Only)
tests.trakCode: Varicella Zoster IGG Antibody / Measles IGG Antibody / Rubella IGG Antibody
tests.container: 5.5 mL White-topped Serum Monovette (no anticoagulant)
tests.sampleType: Clotted blood (serum)
tests.tat: VZV IgG: 24 hours | Measles/Rubella IgG: Urgent (pregnancy/exposure) 24h; Non-urgent batch 14 days
tests.resamplingInterval: Do not repeat if previously documented immune
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Pregnancy status & gestational age, exact date & nature of rash contact (household/face-to-face), vaccination history.
rejectionTriggers: Serology requested to diagnose ACUTE measles, mumps, or rubella (must use throat swab in MSS for PCR)
tests.collectionNotes: Serology determines IMMUNITY only. For pregnant contacts, check if booking antenatal serum is already stored in the lab before taking new blood. For acute suspected Measles/Mumps/Rubella, discuss with Duty Microbiologist and send throat swab in MSS for PCR.

tests.name: Acute Measles, Mumps or Rubella Viral PCR
tests.trakCode: Measles PCR / Mumps PCR / Rubella PCR
tests.referralLab: West of Scotland Specialist Virology Centre, Glasgow Royal Infirmary
tests.container: Molecular Sampling Solution (MSS - red-capped vial; REMOVE SWAB)
tests.sampleType: Throat swab (or buccal swab for mumps) in MSS
tests.tat: Urgent referred test (24-72 hours once approved)
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Fever/rash/parotitis onset date, travel history, contact with confirmed cases, MMR vaccination status.
rejectionTriggers: Not discussed with Duty Consultant Microbiologist
Swab left inside MSS vial
tests.collectionNotes: Discuss with Duty Consultant Microbiologist to arrange urgent WoSSVC testing. Notify Public Health immediately upon clinical suspicion of a notifiable disease.

tests.name: Mucocutaneous Lesion PCR (HSV 1/2, VZV, Syphilis)
tests.trakCode: Herpes simplex PCR / VZ PCR / Syphilis PCR
tests.referralLab: West of Scotland Specialist Virology Centre, Glasgow Royal Infirmary
tests.container: Molecular Sampling Solution (MSS - red-capped vial; REMOVE SWAB)
tests.sampleType: Swab of deroofed vesicle base or ulcer exudate in MSS
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Anatomical site of vesicle/ulcer, immunocompromised/pregnancy status, suspected shingles/HSV/chancre.
rejectionTriggers: Swab left inside MSS vial
Charcoal bacterial swab sent for viral PCR
tests.collectionNotes: Deroof vesicle or rub ulcer base firmly with dry swab, swirl in MSS for 30s, express fluid, and discard swab before capping.

tests.name: Chlamydia trachomatis & Neisseria gonorrhoeae (CT/GC) PCR
tests.container: Abbott MultiCollect Kit (orange-topped tube with orange swab / urine pastette)
tests.sampleType: Biological Male: First-catch urine (via pastette) | Biological Female: Low Vaginal Swab (urine NOT accepted) | Extragenital: Eye/Rectal/Throat swab
tests.volume: Fill urine window between min/max lines using pastette
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Anatomical site, symptomatic vs asymptomatic screen, sexual contact history.
rejectionTriggers: Female urine sample sent for CT/GC PCR (automatically rejected—must be Low Vaginal Swab)
Heavy faecal contamination on rectal swabs or speculum lubricant used (inhibits PCR)
Repeat within 14 days
tests.collectionNotes: Moisten vaginal speculum with water only (lubricants inhibit PCR). For biological males, transfer first-catch urine into the orange-topped MultiCollect tube using the supplied pastette. Note: Rectal LGV testing is referred to SBSTIRL Edinburgh.

tests.name: T-SPOT.TB Assay (Interferon-Gamma Release Assay / IGRA)
tests.referralLab: Oxford Immunotec / Oxford Diagnostics, Oxford
tests.container: Orange-topped Sarstedt Lithium Heparin Monovette (T-SPOT tube)
tests.sampleType: Whole heparinised blood (strictly ambient temperature)
tests.volume: Adults & >10 yrs: 1 x 5.5 mL | 2-9 yrs: 1 x 4 mL | <2 yrs: 1 x 2 mL
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: MANDATORY: Exact date & time of venepuncture, pre-biologic/anti-TNF screening or TB contact history.
rejectionTriggers: Arrives at Crosshouse after 14:00 Mon-Fri (cannot make courier to reach Oxford within 32-hour viability window)
Taken on Friday afternoon, weekend, or bank holiday
Refrigerated or frozen (kills T-lymphocytes)
Missing exact collection time
tests.collectionNotes: CRITICAL TIMING: Must arrive at Crosshouse Microbiology NO LATER THAN 14:00 Mon-Fri so it reaches Oxford within 32 hours of venepuncture. Keep strictly at ROOM TEMPERATURE—do NOT refrigerate. Cannot exclude active TB.

tests.name: High Consequence Infectious Diseases (HCID / VHF / Ebola / MERS)

tests.container: DO NOT SAMPLE WITHOUT CONSULTANT MICROBIOLOGIST & IPC INSTRUCTION
tests.sampleType: Protocol-specific (e.g. 5.5 mL serum + 7.5 mL EDTA for VHF)
tests.clinicalDetailsRequired: Travel to endemic/outbreak region within 21 days, fever/symptoms, PPE/isolation status.
rejectionTriggers: ANY sample sent without prior Consultant Microbiologist agreement and safe-sampling instructions
Sent via pneumatic tube
tests.collectionNotes: STOP: Follow NHS A&A HCID Plan immediately. Isolate patient, apply strict PPE, and contact Duty Consultant Microbiologist BEFORE taking any blood or swabs.
